profile.address: 1807, Michael Faraday Court, Reston Station, Reston, Fairfax County, Virginia, 20190
profile.reading:
Evocative IAD1 occupies a single building at 1807 Michael Faraday Court in Reston, Virginia, an address the operator's own current facility page confirms alongside a description of the site as a Tier III edge data center with two 200 kVA redundant utility transformers, roughly 400 kVA of total electrical service, and 14 thirty ton CRAC cooling units. That operator confirmed detail describes a comparatively small, edge oriented building rather than a hyperscale campus, consistent with the site's documented history.

The building's ownership history stretches back decades and is unusually well documented in trade press. Data Center Knowledge reported that the facility, built in 1982, was originally an AboveNet property before Digital Realty Trust acquired it in 2006. Digital Realty later sold a larger multi state portfolio including this Reston property to Netrality Properties, and Netrality in turn sold the Virginia assets, including this building and a second former Digital Realty site at 251 Exchange Place in Herndon, to Lincoln Property Company's Lincoln Rackhouse division, in a transaction Data Center Knowledge dated to July 2016. At that time Lincoln Rackhouse described the Reston building as having just over 11,000 square feet of raised floor space and about 1 megawatt of power capacity, up from 900 kilowatts, with the building then only partially occupied.

Evocative, led at the time by chief executive Arman Khalili, entered a long term lease with an option to purchase the property from Lincoln Rackhouse, announced in January 2018 per both Data Center Knowledge and Data Center Dynamics, marking the company's first East Coast facility after earlier 2018 West Coast acquisitions from 365 Data Centers and ColoNet. Those January 2018 trade press reports described the Reston facility's capacity at that time as 25,000 square feet and 2.2 megawatts, expandable to 53,000 square feet and 5.7 megawatts as demand grew. Those trade press figures for overall building capacity do not obviously reconcile with the smaller 400 kVA total electrical service figure stated on Evocative's own current site for this building, and this registry has not been able to resolve that discrepancy from public sources, so both are recorded here rather than one being silently preferred over the other.

Evocative's own site describes itself as a global infrastructure provider operating data center, bare metal, network, cloud, and managed services across 24 data centers in 14 metros and 32 points of presence, claiming SOC 1, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SSAE 18, and ISAE 3402 compliance across its facilities and a carrier neutral posture at this Reston site specifically. The building sits in Reston, Virginia, near the Dulles Technology Corridor and within reach of the dense Ashburn, Virginia colocation and hyperscale cluster that handles a large share of North American internet traffic, though this smaller edge facility is a different class of building from the larger wholesale campuses further out toward Loudoun County. No Fairfax County rezoning or special exception case specific to 1807 Michael Faraday Court was located in this research, plausibly because the building predates modern data center specific zoning categories and has changed hands and operators repeatedly without new construction requiring such review. No square footage or year built figure newer than the trade press history above was found on Evocative's own page, and no county assessor record was consulted this session, so current occupied square footage and any standby or onsite generation capacity remain unconfirmed.

reading.body:
Evocative IAD1 is a 0.4 megawatt edge data center in a single 1982-built building in Reston, Virginia, near the Wiehle-Reston East Metro station. The operator describes the site as Tier III with two 200 kVA redundant utility transformers and 14 thirty-ton CRAC cooling units. Trade press from 2018 reported the building contained 25,000 square feet expandable to 53,000 square feet with capacity up to 5.7 megawatts, figures that do not obviously reconcile with the 400 kVA total electrical service stated on Evocative's current page, and public sources do not resolve this discrepancy.

The facility is certified for SOC 1, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SSAE 18, and ISAE 3402 compliance. At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, the 0.4 megawatt published IT load would support roughly 10 racks, though the operator does not state per-rack power density or current occupancy. The building has been repeatedly re-leased and re-branded as AboveNet, Digital Realty, Netrality, Lincoln Rackhouse, and now Evocative since 2006, with no Fairfax County zoning review findings, consistent with retrofit of an existing structure rather than new ground-up construction.

IAD1 ranks 26th by published capacity among Virginia's 330 mapped facilities and represents 0.025 percent of the state's 1,603.4 megawatts of published capacity. The site sits within the Ashburn colocation and hyperscale corridor but belongs to a different building class than the larger wholesale campuses further into Loudoun County. No organized community opposition to data center use at this address was found in research, plausibly because the building predates modern data center zoning categories.
